Design-based SEM fit

Source: R/class.R
svysem-class.Rd

An object of class svysem is a lavaan::lavaan fit whose standard errors use the survey design. Where the estimator has a scaled test, that test uses the design too. coef(), vcov(), parameterEstimates(), standardizedSolution(), lavaan::lavTestWald() and lavaan::fitMeasures() therefore report design-based results with no further step.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'svysem'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'svysem'
vcov(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'svysem'
coef(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'svysem'
vcov(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'svysem'
show(object)

# S4 method for class 'svysem'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'svysem.summary'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A svysem fit.

...

Passed to the lavaan summary.

x

A summary of a svysem fit.

Value

The class extends lavaan. See svysem() for the fitting functions.

Slots

df

Design degrees of freedom, survey::degf() of the design passed to svysem(), svycfa() or svygrowth().

estimator

Estimator used for the variance. "MLM", "WLSMV", or "MLR".

variance_method

How the variance was estimated. "linearization" for single-group MLM or for MLR on a survey.design, and "replication" for WLSMV, for MLM with group=, or for any estimator on a svyrep.design.

svysem_call

The call to svysem(), svycfa() or svygrowth().

References

Oberski D (2014). "lavaan.survey: An R Package for Complex Survey Analysis of Structural Equation Models." Journal of Statistical Software, 57(1), 1–27. doi:10.18637/jss.v057.i01

See also

svysem(), survey::svydesign(), lavaan::sem()

Examples

design <- simulate_design(n_psu = 6, n_per = 4, n_strata = 2, seed = 1)
fit <- svysem(
  "y ~ x1 + x2", design,
  fixed.x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE
)
fit@df
#> [1] 10
fit@estimator
#> [1] "MLM"
fit@variance_method
#> [1] "linearization"
